primitives.name: Borel Measure Uniqueness
primitives.verbatim_quote: If μo is a Baire measure, then there exists a unique, regular Borel measure μ such that μ(E) = μo(E) for every Baire set E.
primitives.assumptions: Every Baire measure is regular; equality holds on Baire sets.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-uniqueness or non-regularity of Borel extension.

layer2.mapping: Baire measure uniquely extends to regular Borel measure.

The induced measure μ is shown to agree with the original Baire measure μo on Baire sets, leveraging the fact that all Baire measures are regular. This ensures a unique extension to a regular Borel measure, which preserves the measure-theoretic properties of the original space. Failure modes arise when compact sets cannot be separated or when the content does not satisfy regularity conditions, leading to non-uniqueness or non-measurability.
